thread.title: Barron’s Next 50: Meet Some ‘Visionary Leaders’ from Our Companies

title: Barron’s Next 50: Meet Some ‘Visionary Leaders’ from Our Companies
text:
David Marino-Nachison May 30, 2018 11:57 a.m. ET
Fast Company recently named 100 “ visionary leaders ” — Barron’s also just named our top CEOs — who, over the past year, have “accomplished something truly novel over the past year that is having an impact on an entire industry.”
Many of those leaders work at Barron’s Next 50 companies, including (listed below in the order of the magazine’s ranking):
• Tesla (TSLA) Chief Designer Franz von Holzhausen, who said the company wants “to show that an electric vehicle can be better than anything. Not just better than a normal road car, but better than any supercar.” More About Barron’s Next The Barron’s Next 50
• Instagram Director of Business Platform Product Visal Shah, who said the Facebook (FB)-owned company is “shooting for an ad experience that not only feels native, but also helps users discover products or services they would actually love to find out about.”
• Amazon.com (AMZN) VP of Technology Dilip Kumar and VP Gianna Puerini, who have led the creation of the massive digital retailer’s Go cashierless store. Here’s more on that effort . Newsletter Sign-up
• Netflix (NFLX) VP of Product Innovation Chris Jaffe, who discussed his company’s decision not to emphasize long-term promotion of its content — “i—doesn’t seem to resonate,” he said — focusing instead one more in-the-moment tools.
• Google Senior Vice President of Hardware Rick Osterloh, who has been central to the Alphabet -owned (GOOGLE) company’s efforts to become more of a player in consumer electronics.
• Walt Disney (DIS) VP of Technology Nikki Katz, who started a coding “boot camp” for the company’s female employees that is now being rolled out across Disney. Here’s more on that effort .
• Twitter (TWTR) Global Vice President and Head of Content Partnerships Kay Madati, who has helped the company’s push into live video by focusing on partnerships with content creators, rather than attacking them head on.
• Walmart (WMT) VP of Global Ecommerce Incubation Katie Finnegan, whose shopping startup became part of the retail giant through acquisition and how tries to help the company evolve in the face of digital conversation — or what she calls “new verticals, capabilities, and existential threats.”
• Apple (AAPL) VP of Internet Services and Apple Pay Jennifer Bailey, who wants her company be a leader in the shift toward increasingly digital consumer commerce. Here’s more on that effort .
